text:
maya: heads up — i just saw a project from another org show up in my console view (prod user).
maya: quick screenshot attached (img_001).
maya: repro steps: 1) open /console/projects 2) apply my-org quickfilter 3) click into list, see 'Project: Apollo' where org_id = org-b (not mine).
jamie: can you curl the internal API and paste the headers/response?
maya: sure — here's a pared-down request/response we saw from the browser network tab:
```
GET /internal/console/projects?filter=my-quick HTTP/1.1
Host: console.internal
X-Org: org-a
X-Request-ID: 01ABCD
Accept: application/json

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: public, max-age=30
X-Request-ID: 01ABCD
Content-Type: application/json
Body: [{"project_id":"apollo","org_id":"org-b","name":"Apollo"}, ...]
```
karl: looks like the response body contains org_b even though incoming header was org_a. my guess: edge cache key isn't including X-Org so cached response from org-b got served to org-a. we changed cache key rules in the CDN -> path+query only last week.
nina: fwiw the console proxy adds X-Org before calling internal services, but the CDN terminates TLS and caches based on path/query. if the proxy is behind CDN and we don't Vary by X-Org, that's unsafe.
nina: also noticed we return 304 in some cases — a 304 from the origin can drop headers during CDN handling; weird interactions possible.
jamie: i grep'd the logs for request-id 01ABCD — here's the origin log (filtered):
```
origin.request id=01ABCD path=/internal/console/projects user=maya org=org-a
origin.response id=01ABCD status=200 cacheable=true set-cookie= - X-Org=org-b body=projects(3 rows)
```
jamie: origin is somehow building the project row with org-b. could be a DB query scoping bug OR a stale cache shard on the origin side itself.
karl: two independent hypotheses: 1) origin reads projects from a shared cache (memcached/redis) keyed by a non-org-scoped key; 2) origin query uses tenant param from an auth token that can be different from X-Org header.
nina: we recently refactored project list service to split JWT parsing to a shared middleware — maybe a regression there where we prefer header over token or vice-versa.
leo: i can repro locally when i flip the feature flag for the new cache layer. steps for repro (local):
- run docker-compose with redis-foo:6379
- seed redis key projects:list:latest = payload for org-b
- hit /internal/console/projects with X-Org org-a and you get org-b rows.
leo: so origin-level cache key is missing org id.
ops-bot: FYI deploy-bot reports last deployment touching console-projects service: svc/console-projects @ 2026-01-23T14:02 (rollout id r-9981).
jamie: immediate mitigation options:
- disable CDN caching for /internal/console/* (safest, quick)
- include X-Org in CDN cache key (requires infra change + testing)
- enforce server-side cache key namespaced by org (code change)
- short-term: purge cache shards for recently affected orgs
we should also add an assert in the service that org header == org in payload and log/fail loudly in debug stacks.
maya: we need quick mitigation — users are seeing cross-org rows. not acceptable.
karl: i volunteer to add server-side namespacing to the cache keys (console-projects will prefix by org id). takes ~3-4 hours dev + unit tests. recommended canary to 10% first.
nina: i'll own the CDN toggle to disable caching for the route for now (1min change), and then re-enable once code fix and tests are live.
leo: i'll open a small e2e that seeds redis with org-b and asserts org-a never gets that payload.
jamie: long term: i want us to stop relying on X-Org from a header alone — we should have origin derive tenant only from the validated JWT (or require a signed org claim). proposal: require an "org" claim in the access token and ignore user-supplied X-Org at origin unless edge attaches a signed header.
karl: SGTM. for speed, code fix + CDN toggle + e2e should be enough. then we'll follow up with token claim enforcement RFC.
deploy-bot: scheduled rollout: svc/console-projects r-10012 by karl -> canary 10% in 30m -> full 2h if no errors.
jamie: i'll watch telemetry and error budget; also add a quick dashboard: metric crossorg.rows.count and alert if >0 for any org.
maya: thanks — please ping here once CDN toggle is live.
leo: CDN toggle done (disabled caching for /internal/console/*). confirming reduced cache hits.
leo: repro attempt now returns correct org-a rows.
maya: verified in prod UI — Apollo row disappeared from my view.
karl: pushing code now, tests included. will roll out canary.
ops-bot: canary started for svc/console-projects r-10012 -> 10% traffic.
jamie: seeing no cross-org rows in canary traces so far. keeping watch for 30m.
maya: adding a note to postmortems channel and I'll open a small doc on onboarding infra changes that affect cache key semantics.
leo: follow-up tasks: 1) RFC for org claim in tokens (jamie) 2) add unit/integration tests for cache key namespacing (karl) 3) CDN infra change to include org if we ever need cache at CDN level (ina).
maya: thanks team.
leo: assigning karl + jamie for followups, marking thread as resolved after full rollout.
deploy-bot: full rollout completed for r-10012 (status: success).
maya: confirmed resolved from affected user reports and my manual checks.
jamie: i'll keep alerting on crossorg.rows.count for 48h then lower severity.
